title: Cell-body distance improves donor-held-out latency predictions for mouse inhibitory connections in Allen brain-slice data
abstract: We tested whether cell-body distance adds information about response onset latency after cell class and layer are known. We used the Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 small database. We kept all records from each inferred animal or human donor in the same validation fold. The full sample had 2,544 connections from mouse visual cortex and human temporal cortex. Distance reduced prediction error for mouse inhibitory connections from 0.490 to 0.468 ms. An exploratory check within 500 micrometres gave 0.484 and 0.468 ms for 1,327 connections from 516 inferred mice. The paired mean squared error gain was 0.0149 ms squared, with an approximate donor bootstrap interval of 0.0072 to 0.0236. A model with cell-class and layer interactions gave the same direction in ten splits. The other three groups did not show a clear gain within 500 micrometres. Cell-body distance can help set inhibitory timing in this mouse sample. The result does not identify conduction speed or establish a rule across species. Donor labels were inferred from public specimen names, and the intervals condition on fitted prediction models.
